reports.summary: Can follow the assignment structure but still mixes up data flow and struggles to connect runtime errors to the lesson concept.
likelyCauses: Understands the happy path but loses the thread when the output differs from the example.
Needs more practice reading terminal feedback before asking Codex for the next step.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Reinforce the mental model for data flow and run one guided debugging walkthrough.

reports.summary: Comfortable with the coding task and concept, but still hesitant during commit and push steps.
likelyCauses: Git confidence is lagging behind coding confidence.
Needs repetition with the repo workflow rather than more theory.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Give a short Git repetition drill and pair Aisha with a student who needs implementation support.

reports.summary: Gets blocked before writing meaningful code because file navigation and task breakdown are still unclear.
likelyCauses: Does not yet have a stable map of how the repo is organized.
Uses Codex for rescue instead of first identifying the exact file and next edit.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Run a short clinic on repo orientation and force a step-by-step implementation plan before coding.

reports.summary: Much stronger than yesterday. Can debug smaller issues independently, though complex stack traces still slow progress.
likelyCauses: Concept understanding improved after repeated practice.
Needs continued exposure to multi-step debugging rather than new theory.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Keep Noor on the current path and give one stretch debugging exercise.

reports.summary: Understands the lesson well and mostly uses Codex for verification rather than rescue.
likelyCauses: Only minor clarification requests during implementation.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Offer a stretch task or mentoring role during the next shared project.

reports.summary: Improved repo navigation, but still needs support turning assignment instructions into a concrete implementation sequence.
likelyCauses: Can locate files now but still hesitates at the point of deciding the first code change.
Repeatedly asks Codex to choose the next step during ambiguous tasks.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Teach a lightweight planning checklist before implementation starts.

reports.summary: The concept is mostly understood, but workflow friction returns when the task requires branching, commits, and merging alongside coding.
likelyCauses: The student thinks clearly about code changes but slows down when process overhead is added.
Codex is still being used as a workflow crutch during Git steps.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Run a hands-on Git workflow drill tied to the current assignment.

reports.summary: Still performing strongly. Most questions are about edge cases and confirming tradeoffs rather than conceptual confusion.
likelyCauses: Uses Codex as a reviewer, not as an autopilot replacement.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Give Aisha a stretch review task and use her progress as a benchmark for others.

reports.summary: Still loses momentum when the lesson asks for reasoning across multiple files and cannot consistently explain why each code change is needed.
likelyCauses: The core concept is still shaky, so debugging becomes guesswork.
Needs structured prompting rules that force explanation before implementation.
reports.recommendedTutorAction: Re-teach the concept with a smaller example and require Rahul to narrate the next step before coding.
